assessment.title: SAMPLE Week 0 — not for real use
assessment.instructions_md: This is a **sample** Week 0 assessment for platform testing only. Answers are fictional. Allow about two hours; you may pause and return.

sections.title: Knowledge
sections.instructions_md: Multiple-choice and profile questions. Profile answers are not scored.

sections.title: Prompting
sections.instructions_md: Show how you would prompt Claude for a realistic task.

sections.title: Department task
sections.instructions_md: You will see one practical task for your department.

sections.title: Safety and judgement
sections.instructions_md: Choose the safest response and explain your reasoning where asked.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.instructions_md: Describe how AI fits into your day-to-day work.

sections.title: Technical supplement (optional)
sections.instructions_md: Optional. Does not count toward your placement total.

levels.descriptor: Fully on brief for the department.

items.prompt_md: Which tools do you use for work-related AI today? (Select all that apply.)
Have you completed the fictional agency data-rules briefing?
Roughly how many hours per week do you spend on repeatable copy tasks?
What is a **token** in the context of large language models?

options.text: A chunk of text the model reads or writes

items.explanation_md: Models process text as tokens (pieces of words).

items.prompt_md: You need to quote a statistic in a blog post. What is the best first step?

options.text: Ask Claude for the number and paste it
Verify against a primary or client-approved source
Use the highest number to sound impressive

items.explanation_md: Always trace figures to an approved source.

items.prompt_md: A colleague pastes a **fictional** client name into a public chatbot. What do you do?

options.text: Remind them to remove client identifiers and use approved tools

items.prompt_md: When should you attach a **Project** knowledge file in Claude?

options.text: Whenever you want the model to guess policies
When stable reference material should ground answers
Only when the file contains live client PII
When stable reference material should ground answers (full credit)

items.explanation_md: Partial credit option b; best answer is d.

items.prompt_md: Which prompt addition most improves **first-draft** quality for a brief?
Draft a prompt (and show fictional output) to turn bullet notes into a client-ready email summary. Use the **Acme Widgets** fictional brand only.
items.model_answer_md: Prompt names role, audience, tone, length, and a verification step. Output is clearly labelled as fictional.
items.marking_notes_md: Do not penalise brand names that are clearly fictional.

items.prompt_md: Write a prompt to repurpose a fictional blog outline into three LinkedIn posts. Include an editor approval step.
items.model_answer_md: Shows structured prompt and three distinct post drafts with approval note.
items.marking_notes_md: Content boundary: nothing publishes without editor sign-off.

items.prompt_md: Describe how you would use Claude for **copy** for a fictional campaign mood board — not final visuals.
items.model_answer_md: Copy-only; references human designer for visuals.
items.marking_notes_md: Creative boundary: Claude does not produce final visuals.

items.prompt_md: Explain how you would summarise fictional export metrics for a weekly performance email without inventing figures.
items.model_answer_md: Requires pasted metrics and traceable sources.
items.marking_notes_md: Performance boundary: no figure without an export.

items.prompt_md: May you paste **real** employee performance reviews into a public AI tool?

options.text: Yes, if you delete names later
No — use approved tools and redact identifiers

items.prompt_md: A model gives a confident medical claim for a health client. What is safest?
In one or two sentences, how would you handle a request to put **fictional** client secrets into a shared chat?
items.model_answer_md: Decline, use approved tooling, escalate if unsure.
items.marking_notes_md: Look for escalation and no client data in shared chats.

items.prompt_md: Describe one repeatable task you could speed up with AI and where a human would still review the result.
items.model_answer_md: Names task, tool boundary, and review step.

items.prompt_md: (Optional) What does an API **rate limit** usually protect against?

options.text: Too many requests in a short time
